decisions.latin: Parátum cor meum, Deus, parátum cor meum
decisions.why: **Doublet: identical to 56:8a**, so it copies Ps 56's ruling (the *parátus* row, the formula row for 56:8 = 107:2): *pronto*, the plain word for 'ready', the repetition kept whole, the copula supplied (D2). In Ps 107 there is no *paravérunt* in the verse before, so the echo Ps 56 lost with *pronto* does not exist here. The same verse (with 107:2's *psallam in glória mea*) is the Alleluia of Pent20-0, per the formula row.

options.label: preparado
options.note: MS1932; Ps 56's option; heavier by four syllables.

options.label: firme
options.note: the Hebrew's נָכוֹן; refused (rule 1), as in Ps 56.

decisions.why: The bare vocative *Deus*, as in the twins (56:8, 56:12, 59:12) and the finished psalms; Ps 56's stylist asked *ó Deus* and was refused there for the psalter-wide ruling that stays with D44 (flagged for Gustavo). One touch changes all three places here. In 107:12 the second *Deus* (inside the copied colon of 59:12b / 43:10b) is not a slot; it follows whatever 43:10b and 59:12b do.

options.label: ó Deus
options.note: Ps 56's stylist; MS1932; the familiar form.

decisions.why: **The doublet parts here, because the Latin does.** 56:8 and 56:10 have *psalmum dicam (tibi)* → *entoarei um salmo*; 107:2 and 107:4 have the verb *psallam (tibi)*, which is D25's *entoar salmos* (the D25 row names 107:2 as a verse where *psállere* stands beside *cantáre*, which is why the verb cannot be *cantar*). The Greek is ψαλῶ in all four places (Rahlfs, in the parallels files), so D15's test would allow Ps 107 to copy *um salmo*; refused, because the two Latin phrases already have two settled Portuguese forms that differ only in the noun's number, and a reader crossing columns sees a verb here, a noun there. Copying Ps 56 is option 2.

options.label: entoarei um salmo / vos entoarei um salmo
options.note: = 56:8, 56:10 (*psalmum dicam*); the same Greek ψαλῶ; hides the Latin's variation.

decisions.why: Absent from 56:8 (which ends *psalmum dicam*); ἐν τῇ δόξῃ μου. *in* + ablative is open between place/state ('in my glory') and instrument ('with my glory', DRB) — and *glória mea* is the psalmist's self (the *glória mea* row, 56:9 = 107:3, the next verse, where it is called on). *na minha glória* keeps both readings as the Latin does, and keeps the same noun one verse before *minha glória* returns as a vocative. MS1932 *no meio da minha glória* adds *meio*.

options.label: na minha glória
options.note: Ruling; the preposition to the letter; open as the Latin.

options.label: com a minha glória
options.note: DRB 'with my glory'; decides for the instrument.

decisions.latin: Exsúrge, glória mea, exsúrge, psaltérium et cíthara
decisions.why: **Doublet: 107:3 = 56:9 word for word**, so the whole verse is Ps 56's (the formula row says 107:3 copies it; the Epi2-3 versicle). *tu*, the Latin's one singular *exsúrge* said to the glory and to the instruments together (MS1932 the same). Ps 56's ambiguity reader heard *minha glória* as God first; the *vós* reading stays as the option Ps 56 gave it.

options.label: Levanta-te … levantai-vos
options.note: plural for two instruments; breaks the repetition (Ps 56's option).

options.label: Levantai-vos … levanta-te
options.note: Ps 56's ambiguity reader: *minha glória* = God; splits the Latin's one form.

decisions.why: Copied from 56:9 with the Latin's order (the mediant on the proparoxytone *cítara*, as the Latin's on *cíthara*); Ps 56's stylist asked to swap them and was refused there. Identical Latin, identical Portuguese.

options.label: cítara e saltério
options.note: Ps 56's stylist; paroxytone mediant; against the Latin's order.

decisions.latin: Quia magna est super cælos misericórdia tua
decisions.why: **Differs from the twin 56:11** (*Quóniam magnificáta est usque ad cælos*, a verb of becoming great, 'up to' the heavens): here an adjective and a copula (μέγα), and *super* (ἐπάνω, 'above'). So Ps 56's *se engrandeceu até os céus* is not copied; *é grande sobre os céus* says what this Latin says. Ps 56's order is kept — copula first, then the reach, then the subject — so the two verses still sound alike where the Latin is alike, and the second colon is 56:11b word for word. *Quia → porque* (as *Quóniam* in 56:11).

options.label: é grande
options.note: Ruling; the adjective and copula; the order of 56:11.

options.label: grande é
options.note: the adjective first, as the Latin; *Porque grande é* stumbles at the head.

decisions.why: 107:6 copies 56:12 (*Exaltai-vos sobre os céus, Deus*, the formula row), so *super cælos* there is *sobre os céus*. 107:5 has the same Latin words one verse earlier, and one Latin word stays one Portuguese word inside the psalm. The Greek differs (ἐπάνω in 107:5, ἐπί in 107:6, Rahlfs), and DRB and MS1932 both say *above / acima dos céus* in 107:5; but the Latin does not differ, and it is the Latin that is translated. *sobre os céus* in 107:5 can be heard as 'reaching over the heavens', which is the image. The split (*acima* only in 107:5) is option 3.

options.label: sobre os céus (both)
options.note: Ruling; one Latin word, one Portuguese; = 56:12, 8:2b.

options.label: acima dos céus (both)
options.note: Ps 56's option; breaks the copy of 56:12.

options.label: acima (107:5) / sobre (107:6)
options.note: follows the Greek's two prepositions, DRB and MS1932 in 107:5; splits one Latin word.

decisions.latin: Exaltáre super cælos, Deus, et super omnem terram glória tua
decisions.why: **Doublet: the first colon of 107:6 = 56:12 word for word** (the *Exaltáre* row and the formula row: '107:6a copies it'), including *super omnem terram → sobre toda a terra*. The Latin moves the asterisk: 56:12 breaks after *Deus*, 107:6 after *glória tua*, because 107:6 goes on with 59:7a (*ut liberéntur dilécti tui*), which is copied as *para que sejam livrados os vossos amados*. The punctuation follows this Latin (comma after *Deus*).

options.label: Sede exaltado
options.note: the passive to the letter; DRB 'Be thou exalted' (Ps 56's option).

decisions.latin: Salvum fac déxtera tua, et exáudi me
decisions.why: **Doublet: = 59:7b** (capitalised here because it opens the verse). Ps 59 left the Latin's missing object unsupplied (*salvum* is singular, but the verse before speaks of *dilécti tui*); the *me* of *escutai-me* carries over, as in the Latin. Copied with its options.

options.label: Salvai
options.note: Ruling; = 59:7b; no object, as the Latin.

decisions.latin: Deus locútus est in sancto suo
decisions.why: **Doublet: = 59:8a.** Ps 59 v2 took *no seu santo* (the Latin's bare neuter, open between the holy place, the holiness and the holy one) after its Latinist and stylist both found *lugar santo* settled it as a place. Copied; MS1932 here too has *no seu santuário*.

options.label: no seu lugar santo
options.note: Ps 59 draft 1; the *sancta* row; settles a place.

decisions.why: **Differs from the twin 59:8** (*lætábor → eu me alegrarei*). The Latin has another verb here, and the *exsultáre / lætári* row keeps them apart (*exultar / alegrar-se*; 117:24 has both side by side). The Greek differs too, and in an unexpected way: 59:8 has ἀγαλλιάσομαι, 107:8 in Rahlfs ὑψωθήσομαι ('I will be exalted'); the Latin *exsultábo* is not a rendering of the Rahlfs word, so by rule 1 it is followed, not corrected. Without the pronoun: *Exultarei* opens the verse on its own stress, where 59:8's *me alegrarei* needed *eu* to avoid opening on a clitic; the blind readers of other psalms listed *exultar* forms as unknown several times (the row) and it was kept each time.

options.label: Eu exultarei
options.note: 59:8's build (*eu me alegrarei*) with this verb; marks the oracle's first person.

options.label: Serei exaltado
options.note: Rahlfs ὑψωθήσομαι; not the Latin (rule 1); refused.

decisions.why: 59:8 has *partíbor → repartirei*; here *dívidam*. The Greek is one verb in both (διαμεριῶ, Rahlfs), and the open row *partíri / divídere (land)* proposes that 107:8 copy *repartir* (= 21:18 *repartiram*, where the Latin is *divídere*). By D15's test the variation is the Latin translators', with no difference of sense, so the twin's word is kept and the two verses sound alike where they mean alike. *dividirei* is the cognate and shows the variation; option 2.

options.label: repartirei
options.note: Ruling; = 59:8 and 21:18; D15's test (διαμεριῶ in both).

options.label: dividirei
options.note: the cognate; shows the Latin's variation.

decisions.why: = 59:8 (*o vale das tendas*, the *tabernáculum* row; the Latin translates the place name, following the Greek τὴν κοιλάδα τῶν σκηνῶν). The verb differs (*dimétiar* for 59:8's *metíbor*) but the Greek is the same (διαμετρήσω both times), so *medirei* is copied as well; the natural order (verb before object) as in 59:8.

**Differs from the twin 59:9** (*fortitúdo → a força*). *Suscéptio* is the only one in the psalter (grep of the DO Latin); L&S 'a taking in hand … an acceptance'. The Greek differs as well (ἀντίλημψις here, κραταίωσις in 59:9), and ἀντίλημψις is the noun of the family whose agent noun is ἀντιλήμπτωρ, which the Latin renders *suscéptor*. D19 settled *suscéptor → amparo, suscípere → amparar*; *suscéptio* joins them as *o amparo*: Ephraim is what holds up the speaker's head. MS1932 has *a força* in both psalms (he merges them); DRB 'the protection of my head' (*protéctor → protetor* is kept apart by D19).

options.label: o amparo
options.note: Ruling; the D19 family (suscéptor / suscípere); ἀντίλημψις.

options.label: a força
options.note: = 59:9 (*fortitúdo*); MS1932 in both psalms; another Latin word.

options.label: a proteção
options.note: DRB 'protection'; the *protéctor* family, which D19 keeps apart.

decisions.latin: Juda rex meus: * Moab lebes spei meæ.
decisions.why: = 59:9b in build: the Latin is verbless, carrying *est* over from the verse before; the copula supplied (D2), as Ps 59 ruled, DRB and MS1932. The verbless build is the option, as in Ps 59.

options.label: Judá é o meu rei / Moab é

decisions.why: 59:9b has *olla → a panela*; here *lebes*, the same Greek λέβης (Rahlfs, both psalms). The open row *olla / lebes* asked Ps 107 to choose: copy *panela* by D15's test, or take *caldeirão* to show the Latin's variation. L&S *lebes*: 'a copper basin, kettle, caldron, for cooking … a handbasin for washing'. Ruled *panela*: the Greek is one word, the sense (a menial cooking vessel, Moab reduced to kitchen ware) is one, and the twin verse then sounds the same where it means the same, as with *repartirei* (decision `dividam`). The cost is Ps 59's: the blind reader there heard the slang 'clique'. *o caldeirão* is option 2 and is the one to take if Gustavo wants the Latin's two words visible.

options.label: o caldeirão
options.note: L&S 'caldron'; shows the Latin's variation (the row's proposal).

options.label: a bacia
options.note: L&S 'handbasin'; nearer the Hebrew's washpot, which is not the Latin's concern.

options.label: o vaso
options.note: MS1932 (*como que o vaso*); heard as a flowerpot.

decisions.why: = 59:10a word for word; copied (*Sobre a Idumeia*, ἐπί; MS1932 *sobre a Iduméa* in both psalms).
= 59:10a; copied (*calçado*, the generic word, MS1932).

options.label: sandália
options.note: a kind the Latin does not name (Ps 59's option).

decisions.why: **Differs from the twin 59:10b** (*súbditi sunt → a mim estão sujeitos os estrangeiros*). Here the foreigners have *become friends*; Rahlfs has ὑπετάγησαν ('were subjected') in both psalms, so the Latin of 107 departs from that Greek — followed as it stands (rule 1), as DRB ('the aliens are become my friends') and MS1932 (*os estrangeiros tornaram-se meus amigos*) follow it. *mihi … amíci* is read as 'friends to me' = *meus amigos*; *facti sunt* → *se tornaram* (the change of state). *alienígenæ → estrangeiros* (the open row, = 59:10). Natural order, subject first (D2); Ps 59's head *a mim* is not kept, because *a mim se tornaram amigos os estrangeiros* is an inversion for its own sake.

options.label: os estrangeiros se tornaram meus amigos

forms.amici: os estrangeiros se tornaram meus amigos

options.label: a mim se fizeram amigos os estrangeiros

forms.amici: a mim se fizeram amigos os estrangeiros

options.note: the Latin's order and 59:10b's head *a mim*; *fieri* as *fazer-se*; inverted.

options.label: os estrangeiros se fizeram meus amigos

forms.amici: os estrangeiros se fizeram meus amigos

options.note: *fieri → fazer-se*, nearer the verb's root; a little stiffer.

decisions.latin: Quis dedúcet me … quis dedúcet me
decisions.why: **107:11 = 59:11 word for word**; copied whole (D22 *guiar*, the repetition kept; the glossary's *dedúcere* row says 107:11 should copy).

decisions.latin: Nonne tu, Deus, qui repulísti nos, * et non exíbis, Deus, in virtútibus nostris?
decisions.why: The words of 59:12a are copied (*Não sereis vós, Deus, que nos …*: the copula supplied in the future from 107:11's *dedúcet*, Ps 59's reasoning). **Two small differences from the twin, both the Latin's:** (1) 107:12 has a comma after *nos* where 59:12 has a question mark, so the verse is one question running across the asterisk; the Portuguese follows this Latin's punctuation. (2) *exíbis* for 59:12b's *egrediéris*: the same Greek (ἐξελεύσῃ, Rahlfs, both psalms) and the same sense, so *saireis* is copied (D15's test), and the second colon stays 43:10b = 59:12b word for word.
D42 *repéllere → repelir*, = 59:12 (and 59:3, 42:2, 43:10). Two blind readers (Pss 42, 59) did not know *repelistes*; kept under the settled row.

**107:13 = 59:13 word for word**; copied whole (the formula row: *Dai-nos auxílio na tribulação: * porque é vã a salvação do homem*; the Matins antiphon *Da nobis * Dómine auxílium de tribulatióne*). Ps 59's two Latinist runs contradicted each other on *na / contra*; *na* held there and flagged for Gustavo. Whatever he rules moves both psalms.
= 59:14a word for word (the *fácere virtútem* row: *agir com poder*, = 117:16; the row says 107:14 should copy).

choices.107:2: The first colon is 56:8a; the second differs from 56:8b as the Latin does (*psallam in glória mea* for *psalmum dicam*), see `psallam` and `ingloria`. *cantábo → cantarei* as 56:8.
choices.107:3: = 56:9 whole, every word and mark (*eu me levantarei ao amanhecer*, *exsúrgam dilúculo*).
choices.107:4: First colon = 56:10a (*Eu vos darei graças entre os povos, Senhor*, D5). *in natiónibus* for 56:10's *in géntibus*: the same Greek (ἐν ἔθνεσιν, both psalms), so *entre as nações* is copied (the *nátio* row's *nação* and the *gentes* row's *nações* coincide). The Latin closes the verse with a full stop here (56:10 has a colon), followed.
choices.107:5: Second colon = 56:11b (*e até as nuvens a vossa verdade*), with this Latin's trailing colon, since the sentence runs on into 107:6.
choices.107:6: First colon = 56:12 (with this Latin's comma after *Deus*); second colon = 59:7a (*para que sejam livrados os vossos amados*), lowercase since it continues the sentence. The first colon is long (the Latin's is too: two members before the asterisk).
choices.107:7: *et exáudi me → e escutai-me* (D3), = 59:7b. The Latin's trailing colon kept: the oracle follows in 107:8.
choices.107:8: *dimétiar → medirei* (= 59:8 *metíbor*, the same Greek διαμετρήσω). The Latin's comma at the mediant kept.
choices.107:9: First colon = 59:9a (*Meu é Galaad, e meu é Manassés*); the names in their Vulgate-family forms as Ps 59. The copula *é* before *o amparo* as 59:9 supplies it before *a força*.
choices.107:10: DO numbers two verses 107:10; the second is kept as `107:10b`, as Ps 59 did with its two 59:9.
choices.107:12: Second colon = 43:10b = 59:12b (*e não saireis, Deus, com as nossas forças*; *virtútes nostræ → forças*, D43), *exíbis* for *egrediéris* (see `nonne`).
choices.107:14: First colon = 59:14a. **Differs from 59:14b** where the Latin does: *inimícos nostros → os nossos inimigos* (the *inimíci* row), where 59:14 has *tribulántes nos → os que nos atribulam*; the Greek differs too (τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ἡμῶν / τοὺς θλίβοντας ἡμᾶς, Rahlfs). *ipse → ele mesmo* and *ad níhilum dedúcet → reduzirá a nada* copied.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps107.md (no Diurnal section: Ps 107 is not in the day hours). Ps 107 is the doublet 56:8–12 + 59:7–14; both twins are at v2, reviewed. Each Latin colon compared with its twin in the DO Latin (Psalm56.txt, Psalm59.txt) and the twins' prayed.json/prayed.vos.json and glossary_rows.json read: identical Latin copies the twin's Portuguese exactly (107:3, 107:11, 107:13 whole; half-verses 107:2a, 4a, 5b, 6a, 6b–7a, 7b, 9a, 10, 10b-a, 12, 14a). Divergences, each the Latin's and each a decision: *psallam (in glória mea)* for *psalmum dicam* (107:2, 4), *Quia magna est super* for *Quóniam magnificáta est usque ad* (107:5), *exsultábo* for *lætábor* (107:8; Rahlfs ὑψωθήσομαι, not followed), *dívidam / dimétiar* for *partíbor / metíbor* (same Greek, copied), *suscéptio* for *fortitúdo* (107:9, → *amparo*, D19 family), *lebes* for *olla* (same Greek, copied *panela*), *amíci facti sunt* for *súbditi sunt* (107:10b; departs from Rahlfs ὑπετάγησαν, followed), *exíbis* for *egrediéris* (same Greek, copied), *inimícos nostros* for *tribulántes nos* (107:14). Glossary rows read via ps059/gloss_grep.py.

Hard checks pass (ids 107:2–14 with 107:10b; every mark). Soft length flags, all accepted: 107:2a +5, 107:3b +5, 107:6b +4, 107:7b −4, 107:8b −4, 107:10 second colon (*Moab é a panela…*) +6, 107:12b −3, 107:13a −4 — every one of these cola is copied word for word from the twin (56:8–9, 56:12 + 59:7–13), where the same flags were read and accepted, and identical Latin must give identical Portuguese (rule 6). 107:2b +3 is D25's two words for *psallam*. 107:14b +3 is 59:14b's colon with *os nossos inimigos* for *os que nos atribulam*; one breath. No rhyme flags.
